summary: This article explains how to build a balanced plate with vegetables and fruit, grains, protein, and dairy, and why each food group matters for a healthy body.
introduce: Draw a simple cause → effect arrow on the board and ask students for an everyday example, such as “I did not sleep, so I felt tired.” Tell them that while reading “A Balanced Plate” they will find at least two cause-and-effect links.

keyTerms.def: a useful substance in food that helps the body live and grow
the amount of a food that one person eats
a part of plant foods that helps the body digest food

challengeTerms.def: natural substances in food that the body needs in small amounts to stay healthy
natural substances, such as iron and calcium, that the body needs from food
to break down food in the body so it can be used

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that it is fine to eat sweets every day if you also eat vegetables? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Plan a balanced dinner for your family.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review nutrient, portion, and fiber, and let weak readers match cause cards to effect cards from the article with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use vitamins, minerals, and digest in a short paragraph that explains one important cause-and-effect chain from the article.
